title: standardize-build-matrix-and-inline-toolchain-shims
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem:
Our mono-repo and several language-specific repos each run bespoke CI matrices and rely on ad-hoc global tool installs in builder images. This causes long cold builds, DRY violations in CI definitions, and frequent blips when tool versions drift (linters, formatters, protoc, grpc tools). We've accrued technical debt: inconsistent caching, duplicate layer churn across images, and brittle 'install on every run' steps that amplify CI time and cost.

Goal:
- Reduce CI variance by standardizing a compact build matrix and a canonical set of runtime profiles (slim, standard, full).
- Replace global installs with repo-local inline toolchain shims (per-build tool bundles) to make CI hermetic and cacheable.
- Improve cache hit rates and developer iteration time by priming layer caches and rationalizing image layering.
- Upgrade core linters/toolchains (eslint@8.x, gopls/go-toolchain, rustfmt) behind opt-in per-repo gates and a compatibility test suite.

Scope / Out of scope:
In scope: Docker base image layout for CI builders, multi-stage Dockerfiles for priming, CI job templates (Buildkite + GH Actions), inline toolchain shims and cache configuration, linter/toolchain upgrades in sample repos, observability hooks (build-time metrics).
Out of scope: full migration of every microservice in first rollout, production runtime quantization changes, on-prem packaging changes for Private deployments.

Proposed approach:
1) Define three canonical builder profiles and publish RFC documenting layers and intended uses (slim: test-only, standard: build+unit, full: integration/crosscompile).
2) Create an "inline toolchain shim" specification: a small tarball of tools checked into a new .toolchain/ directory per repo (or built by a dedicated job) that is installed into /usr/local/bin during the early Docker build stage and cached as a layer.
3) Implement shared CI templates that reference the profiles; add a one-line feature flag in repo CI to opt into the new templates.
4) Replace long-running 'apt-get && curl | bash' installs with the shim approach; for languages with native tool managers (go, npm, cargo) use lockfile-driven installs to the shim.
5) Create layer-priming jobs that warm caches in the remote CAS/registry after image build and before heavy rollout.
6) Run parallel compatibility tests for upgraded linters/toolchains using matrixed jobs against a curated set of repos and representative large PRs.

Acceptance criteria:
- New builder images produce at least 30% median build-time reduction for unit test jobs across 10 representative repos.
- Cache hit rate for builder layers improves by 20% within two weeks of rollout (measured via CI cache metrics).
- At least 5 key repos migrated to using inline toolchain shims and the shared templates without flaky regressions after 2 weeks.
- Linter upgrades proceed with an opt-in compatibility job; no repo is auto-upgraded without owner sign-off.

Migration plan / rollout:
Phase 1 (Week 0-2): Ship RFC and canonical images; create CI templates and diagnostic jobs. Pilot on 3 low-risk repos (infra, docs, shared-libs).
Phase 2 (Week 3-6): Instrument metrics, run compatibility matrix for linters and toolchains, iterate on shim packaging. Migrate 5 additional repos (sdk, console-frontend, runner).
Phase 3 (Week 7-12): Broad rollout with automation to suggest per-repo profile and PRs to adopt templates. Gate full rollout with flakiness and cost targets.

Technical notes and tradeoffs:
- Inline toolchain shims increase repo size slightly; we mitigate by generating tarballs in an artifacts bucket and referencing them in builds when appropriate.
- Using layered priming reduces cold-starts but requires extra build steps and a small increase in registry storage. We will set TTLs and pruning.
- We deliberately avoid a single 'monorepo builder image' for all cases to keep image sizes reasonable for CI runners with lower disk. Profiles strike a balance between size and completeness.

Observability and metrics:
- Track median/95th build duration, cache hit rate, CI CPU/GPU minutes, and number of flaky CI runs per repo.
- Add tags to builds (profile=slim|standard|full, shim=enabled) to allow per-profile analysis.

Rollbacks / Safety:
- Template is opt-in by default. If a repo reports >10% increase in flakiness or build time regression we auto-create a revert PR and mark the repo as blocked for 72 hours.
- Toolchain upgrades are gated by compatibility jobs; failing jobs will not flip the repo-level flag.

notes: Consider adding a lightweight language-agnostic 'toolbox' binary to help with deterministic installs inside the shim.
Investigate integrating with existing CAS to deduplicate identical shim tarballs across repos.
Document PR checklist items: add .toolchain/manifest, update CI feature flag, run compatibility job, add owner approval.
Estimate assumes 2 engineers ~50% time for 6 weeks for core work and pilots.
Follow-up ticket suggested to automate generation of .toolchain manifests from lockfiles.
Avoid touching production runtime images in this ticket; keep focus on CI/builder images to reduce blast radius.
